name: ADP7182AUJZ-R7
title: ADP7182: -28 V input, -200 mA, low-noise negative linear regulator
summary: A CMOS low-dropout regulator for negative rails: it takes -2.7 V to -28 V in and delivers up to -200 mA. Fixed versions give -1.2 V to -5 V with 18 µV rms output noise whatever the voltage; the adjustable version sets anything from -1.22 V down to -27 V (or -VIN + VDO) with two resistors on ADJ. It is stable with a 2.2 µF ceramic output capacitor, its EN pin switches it on from either a positive or a negative level of 2 V magnitude, and it has current limiting and thermal shutdown. Packages are a 5-lead TSOT, a 2 mm × 2 mm 6-lead LFCSP and a 3 mm × 3 mm 8-lead LFCSP.
key_figures: fixed -1.2 V to -5 V; adjustable -1.22 V to -27 V
18 µV rms typ, 10 Hz to 100 kHz (fixed output)
66 dB typ at 10 kHz, VOUT = -3 V
-33 µA typ no load; -650 µA typ at -200 mA
±1% at 25 °C; +2% / -3% over line, load and temperature
2.2 µF ceramic, ESR 0.001 Ω to 0.2 Ω

notes: Z in a model number marks a RoHS-compliant part.
Other output voltages are made to special order.

Note 2: dropout is the input-to-output difference with the input set equal to the nominal output voltage; it is specified only for outputs below -3 V.
Note 3: start-up time runs from the rising edge of EN until VOUT reaches 90% of nominal.
Note 4: the current limit is the load at which the output has fallen to 90% of its typical value; for a -5 V output, the current that pulls it to -4.5 V.

tables.title: Input and output capacitance, recommended
notes: Note 1: across every operating condition of the application the effective input and output capacitance must stay above 1.5 µF; choose parts with that in mind. X7R and X5R dielectrics are recommended; Y5V and Z5U are not recommended for any LDO.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: Every rating is a limit on its own; two at once are not implied. Junction temperature beyond its range can damage the part, and the ambient figure does not by itself fix the junction temperature: with high dissipation on a board of high thermal resistance the ambient limit falls, and with modest dissipation on a board of low thermal resistance the ambient may go higher, as long as TJ stays within -40 °C to +125 °C.

circuits.title: Fixed output, VOUT = -5 V
circuits.description: A fixed -5 V version run from -8 V. One 2.2 µF ceramic sits between ground and the input, another between ground and the output. EN is driven from a control line: +2 V or -2 V switches the output on, 0 V switches it off. The NC pin is left open.

parts.value: EN: on at 2 V or -2 V, off at 0 V

circuits.title: Adjustable output, VOUT = -5 V
circuits.description: The adjustable version run from -8 V and set to -5 V by a divider: 40.2 kΩ from VOUT to ADJ and 13 kΩ from ADJ to ground (-1.22 V × (1 + 40.2/13) ≈ -5 V). Input and output each have a 2.2 µF ceramic to ground, and EN takes the ±2 V on / 0 V off control.

parts.value: EN: on at 2 V or -2 V, off at 0 V

circuits.title: Setting the adjustable output, VOUT = -2.44 V
circuits.description: The adjustable version from -3 V with two equal 120 kΩ resistors, VOUT to ADJ and ADJ to ground, giving -2.44 V. With the typical 10 nA ADJ current the two resistors in parallel (60 kΩ) add a 0.6 mV error. Input and output carry 2.2 µF each; EN takes the ±2 V on / 0 V off control.

parts.value: EN: on at 2 V or -2 V, off at 0 V

circuits.title: Adjustable -15 V output with noise reduction network
circuits.description: The adjustable version from -16 V set to -15 V by 147 kΩ (VOUT to ADJ) and 13 kΩ (ADJ to ground). A 13 kΩ resistor in series with 100 nF, from ADJ to VOUT, sits across the upper resistor and cuts the error amplifier's gain above about 10.8 Hz, bringing the output noise down from 220 µV rms to 35 µV rms at -200 mA. Input and output carry 2.2 µF each; EN takes the ±2 V on / 0 V off control.

parts.value: EN: on at 2 V or -2 V, off at 0 V

operation.text: Stock fixed voltages: -5 V in the 3 mm × 3 mm LFCSP; -1.8 V, -2.5 V, -3 V and -5 V in the TSOT; -1.2 V, -1.5 V, -2.5 V and -5 V in the 2 mm × 2 mm LFCSP. Others are available to special order. The fixed versions have 18 µV rms output noise at any voltage.

Inside are a reference, an error amplifier, a feedback divider and an NMOS pass device carrying the load current. When the feedback node sits more positive than the reference, the amplifier drives the NMOS gate toward GND so it conducts harder and the output rises; when it sits more negative, the gate goes toward -VIN and the output falls. The ESD protection appears in the block diagrams as Zener diodes. In the fixed versions the amplifier runs at unity gain with the reference equal to the output, which keeps noise very low; the adjustable version uses a fixed reference with gain set by the output voltage, so its noise scales with the output.
Quiescent current is -650 µA typical at full load; shutdown current is at most -8 µA at room temperature.

RFB1 (VOUT to ADJ) and RFB2 (ADJ to GND) set the output between -1.22 V and -27 V. Keep RFB2 below 120 kΩ so the ADJ leakage does not produce a large output error. About 100 pF across RFB1 can improve stability; a larger capacitor there also lowers noise and raises PSRR.

Designed for small ceramic capacitors, but other types work if their ESR is controlled, since ESR affects loop stability. Use at least 2.2 µF with ESR of 0.2 Ω or less. More output capacitance improves the response to large load steps.

2.2 µF from VIN to GND makes the circuit less sensitive to board layout, particularly with long input traces or a high source impedance. If the output carries more than 2.2 µF, raise the input capacitance to match.

Any good ceramic that meets the minimum capacitance and maximum ESR can be used. X5R or X7R rated 25 V or 50 V is recommended; Y5V and Z5U are not. A larger case or higher voltage rating loses less capacitance under DC bias; the capacitance against DC bias curve is for a 0805, 2.2 µF, 25 V X5R part. X5R varies about ±15% over -40 °C to +85 °C, independent of case size or rating. DC bias, temperature and tolerance together set the worst-case effective capacitance for each design.

EN works with either polarity: the output turns on when |VEN| is 2 V or more, positive or negative relative to ground, and off when EN is at 0 V. Connect EN to VIN for automatic start-up. When disabled, about 220 kΩ inside pulls VOUT up to GND. The thresholds have hysteresis, which stops noise on EN causing on/off chatter; the thresholds are given against VIN from -2.7 V to -28 V.

An internal soft start limits inrush when the output is enabled. For the -5 V option the output reaches 90% of its final value about 450 µs after EN crosses its threshold; start-up time depends on the output voltage.

operation.topic: Noise reduction of the adjustable version
operation.text: Adding RNR and CNR in series across RFB1 lowers the error amplifier's AC gain and brings the adjustable part's noise close to that of a fixed part. With RNR about equal to RFB2 the AC gain is held to roughly 6 dB, so the amplifier always runs above unity gain. CNR sets where the gain falls 3 dB below its DC value. With RFB1 = 147 kΩ, RFB2 = RNR = 13 kΩ and CNR = 100 nF at -15 V: DC gain 12.3 (21.8 dB); 3 dB roll-off 10.8 Hz; high-frequency AC gain 1.92 (5.67 dB); noise reduction factor 6.41 (16.13 dB); measured noise at -200 mA 220 µV rms without the network and 35 µV rms with it; calculated 34.5 µV rms with it. The reduction is largest between 100 Hz and 30 kHz.

The output current is limited at -350 mA typical; beyond that the output voltage drops to hold the current constant. Above 150 °C junction temperature (typical) the output switches off; it switches back on below 135 °C. With VOUT shorted to ground the part first conducts -350 mA, heats past 150 °C, shuts off, cools below 135 °C and restarts, so the current cycles between -350 mA and 0 mA for as long as the short lasts. These protections are for accidental faults: keep the junction at or below 125 °C by limiting dissipation.

Dissipation is usually small, but with high ambient temperature and a large input-output difference the junction can exceed 125 °C. θJA depends on the package materials and on how much copper the VIN pins are soldered to; more copper and planes under the package help, with diminishing returns. TJ against dissipation is given for several copper areas and ambients; when the board temperature TB is the known quantity, ΨJB applies instead. ΨJB is not a thermal resistance: it includes heat leaving the top of the package by convection and radiation (JESD51-8, JESD51-12).

Put the input capacitor close to VIN and GND and the output capacitor close to VOUT and GND. 1206 or 0805 capacitors and resistors give the smallest footprint where area is tight. On the LFCSP the exposed pad connects to the VIN plane. Example evaluation-board layouts exist for the 6-lead LFCSP, 8-lead LFCSP and 5-lead TSOT.
